observable_outcome: The transitions the domain models get a caller outside a test. Measured at 81eef87: RequirementWait, Recover, Evaluate, Start, Pause and Cancel each have ZERO non-test occurrences outside internal/domain/model.go; service.go:993 is the only non-test line constructing a domain.Increment and its only non-test caller is orchestrator.go:59, whose Orchestrator is built only at orchestrator_test.go:65 and :139; release.Pipeline.Promote (pipeline.go:38) has zero non-test callers, so domain.StableReleaseProof (sole constructor domain/release.go:150) is unobtainable in any running process. ONE MECHANISM REPAIRS ALL THREE. api.go:114 already mints the scheduler identity via application.LoopCaller and api.go:119 carries it into the InternalReconcile closure at cmd/control-plane/main.go:199-207; Plan (service.go:888) and Prepare (:1023) already admit RoleScheduler. So: one bounded pass, Service.LoopPass, in new file internal/application/loop.go, gated callerActor(ctx, RoleScheduler) alone, four stages each carrying its justifying observation. A ready Requirement whose scheduler reason is resource-conflict or no-runner-capacity moves to waiting. An active or waiting Requirement with an Execution in domain.ExecutionLost moves to recovering. A ready Requirement the scheduler assigned gets an Increment planned and prepared -- which is what lets claims:acquire and /v1/executions/* succeed at all. Only the proof release.Pipeline.Promote returns carries a Requirement whose Increments all reached released through evaluating to completed, in one transaction. cmd/runner stops being a stub: a real mode reads a capped page from one new runner-role route GET /v1/runner/work, claims what it was offered over real HTTP, starts the Execution, heartbeats once, then STOPS at the provider boundary, posting no result it did not obtain. RunFakeJourney stays test-only and byte-unchanged. The claim stops at preview-local, at component grade for completion.
acceptance_criteria: A1. THE SCOPE-BOUNDARY TABLE IS WRITTEN INTO THE EVIDENCE RECORDS BEFORE ANY SOURCE FILE IS EDITED, AND THE FIRST COMMIT IS THE RECORDS. Five rows, each a list, not a sentence: (1) what this makes true; (2) what it deliberately does not do; (3) what it records but does not fix; (4) what only a later task can establish; (5) whether it passes any release gate -- the answer to (5) is NO, this task passes no gate and issues no gate verdict. V2-085, V2-086 and V2-080 all did this correctly and their first commit is the records; V2-087's single miss was doing it after the edits. REVISION IS PERMITTED (v2-task-dag.md 12.3): if you must widen the boundary, record the PRE-REVISION table verbatim, the revision time and the revision reason in the same evidence record, then widen it in place. Widening in place is PREFERRED over proposing a new task -- do not propose a task id, and do not defer a finding to a task that does not exist. M5's remediation budget stands at 5 of 5 (12.7, 12.10), so a sixth task is a signal that the milestone is mis-cut, not an output of this work.

A2. RE-MEASURE THE BASELINE YOURSELF; EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS EXPECTED TO BE STALE. Each was read by the designer at HEAD 81eef87 with the command given; V2-085 found twelve disagreements and V2-086 found nineteen. Report BOTH values for every disagreement and use the measured one. (i) `grep -rn '\b<name>\b' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go | grep -v internal/domain/model.go` for each of RequirementWait, RequirementRecover, RequirementEvaluate, RequirementStart, RequirementPause, RequirementCancel, RequirementReadyCommand, RequirementStartFraming, RequirementNeedInput and CompleteRequirementFromRelease -- expected 0,0,0,0,0,0,3,3,2,1. (ii) `grep -rn 'domain.Increment{' --include='*.go' internal | grep -v _test.go` -- expected exactly internal/application/service.go:993. (iii) `grep -rn 'RunFakeJourney\|Orchestrator{' --include='*.go' .` -- expected 3 call sites and 2 composite literals, all in internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go. (iv) `grep -rn '\.Promote(\|PromotionGate(' --include='*.go' internal cmd | grep -v _test.go` -- expected only the definitions and the internal delegation at internal/release/pipeline.go:52,59, i.e. zero non-test callers of Pipeline.Promote. (v) `grep -rn 'AttachReleaseObserver\|NewSourceReleaseObserver' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go` -- expected only internal/application/release_surface.go:51 and :121. (vi) `grep -ln 'net/http' internal/runner/*.go` -- expected NO output. (vii) `grep -rn 'httptest.NewServer' --include='*_test.go' . | wc -l` -- expected 0. (viii) `find . -name '*.go' -not -name '*_test.go' | wc -l` -- expected 93, which is the count V2-086's scan asserts over. (ix) The constants: internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:15 MaxCandidates=100; internal/application/readmodels.go:19 MaxPageSize=100; internal/application/allocation.go:93 AllocationLeaseBound=100; internal/reconciler/reconciler.go:17 MaxBatch=100 (the DECLARATION-GAP ledger says :16 -- the designer measured :17, so this one is ALREADY a known disagreement: re-measure and report); internal/quota/quota.go:46 DefaultBudget{25000,10000,10000}, :54 MaxReadBoundaryReads=6000, :56 ReadTransactionUsage{6001,1}, :62 MutationUsage{32,16}. (x) `devbox run --pure -- sh <script>` running `go test -list '.*' <pkg> | grep -c '^Test'` -- expected application 196, api 71, domain 54, reconciler 16, runner 120, release 47, scheduler 26, contracts 33, store/memory 16, quota 14. (xi) internal/store/memory/store.go:353 calls quota.Counter.TrueUp, the same correction internal/store/firestore/store.go:495 applies -- V2-087 landed, so a read/write count measured against the in-memory adapter is meaningful; confirm and report, because V2-084's A15 asserted the opposite and is now stale.

A3. DERIVE THE PRODUCT AUTHORITY FIRST AND STOP IF YOUR READING DIFFERS. Quote each with file and line: docs/architecture/domain-model.md:265 ready = '優先順位評価済みで実行可能'; :266 active = '1つ以上のIncrementが進行中'; :267 waiting = 'dependency、capacity、time条件を自動待機'; :270 recovering = 'lost ExecutionやPreview failureから再開中'; :271 evaluating = 'Stableで課題が解決したか評価中'; :272 completed = '対応Stable ReleaseとEvidenceで課題解決を確認'; :275 'failedをRequirementの終端状態にしない。failureはExecution、Provider Run、Evidenceに記録し、Requirementはrecovering、waiting、needs-inputのいずれかになる。'; :101 '1 Requirementに複数Incrementを許す。Incrementが成功してもRequirementは自動完了しない。'; docs/product/user-facing-spec.md:272 waiting = '外部資源、依存、時間条件などを待ち、自動的に再評価される'; :275 recovering = 'failureまたはRunner消失後、安全な再開を行っている'; docs/product/definition.md:105 '対象変更がPreviewで実証され、Stableへ昇格した時点とする'; :111 '3. 利用可能なworkerが、実行可能なRequirementを排他的にclaimする。'; :130 '完了を自己申告だけで決めず、要求と不変条件を検証する'. State the four conclusions plainly in the evidence: waiting is justified by a capacity or contention or dependency condition; recovering is justified by a lost Execution or a lost Runner; completion is bound to a Stable promotion and is NEVER granted by an Increment succeeding; and an Increment existing at all is the precondition for the whole claim surface. If your reading differs, STOP and escalate; do not implement a different rule and do not implement none.

A4. THE PASS. Add Service.LoopPass to the NEW file internal/application/loop.go. Signature: LoopPass(ctx context.Context, req LoopPassRequest) (LoopPassReport, error). (a) Gate: callerActor(ctx, RoleScheduler) and that role ALONE -- assert ErrForbidden for an owner Caller and for a runner Caller and ErrUnauthenticated for a context with no Caller. Construct NO application.Caller anywhere in the file: internal/application/caller.go is prohibited and application.LoopCaller stays the single sanctioned producer. (b) One clock read per invocation: now := s.clock.Now(), refused if zero, and that ONE instant is passed to every stage and to every domain command's At. (c) LoopPassRequest carries a RequestID namespace and an opaque Cursor and NOTHING else -- no control revision, no repository id, no timestamp, no limit override, and no field that lets a caller pick which Requirement moves. (d) LoopPassReport reports, per stage, the number of transitions issued, the per-stage cap, RequirementsExamined, MoreRequirementsExist, the NextCursor, and for the promotion stage one of promoted / refused-with-reason / skipped-not-configured. (e) Every stage's write path goes through the existing s.mutate/s.record discipline with an idempotency key derived from the request namespace, the stage name and the aggregate id, so a repeated tick with the same namespace replays rather than re-transitions. (f) Do NOT call allocationReport: it discards the page's `more` flag at internal/application/allocation.go:603 and internal/application/allocation.go is prohibited. Build the snapshot from your own u.RequirementsPage(ctx, req.Cursor, scheduler.MaxCandidates) call, keeping BOTH return values, then reuse the EXISTING exported helpers BuildAllocationSnapshot, AllocationSchedulerStatus, AllocationContentionKey and AllocationCreatedAt unchanged.

A5. STAGE W (waiting), with the reason set DERIVED and CLOSED. Issue domain.RequirementWait for a Requirement whose domain status is domain.RequirementReady and whose scheduler.Decision has Assigned == false and Reason in exactly {scheduler.ReasonResourceConflict, scheduler.ReasonNoRunnerCapacity}. Write the switch over ALL SEVEN members of scheduler.AllReasons with an explicit arm and an explicit comment per excluded arm: not-ready (not a condition being awaited, and its Requirements are in statuses domain.DecideRequirement refuses RequirementWait from -- internal/domain/model.go:490-493 admits ready, active, recovering only); already-owned (the Requirement holds an active Lease, i.e. work in flight); unmet-dependency, repository-unavailable and not-executable (UNREACHABLE from BuildAllocationSnapshot -- the rows at internal/application/allocation.go:460-467 carry no Dependencies, Snapshot.Repositories is one synthetic entry with no FailureCount and no IsolatedUntil, and Assessment is never set -- re-measure each and record). Assert with a table over all seven reasons which two transition and which five do not, and assert len(scheduler.AllReasons) == 7 so that a reason added to internal/scheduler fails here rather than silently joining or leaving the set. RECORD, and do not assert, that RequirementWait from active and from recovering stays UNISSUED because AllocationSchedulerStatus (allocation.go:382-392) maps active to StatusAssigned and every other status to the empty status, and scheduler.structurallyReady (scheduler.go:192-202) requires StatusReady, so the scheduler can never attach a capacity or contention reason to them.

A6. STAGE R (recovering), with the observation the shipped reconciler already writes. Issue domain.RequirementRecover for a Requirement whose status is domain.RequirementActive or domain.RequirementWaiting and for which at least one Execution belonging to one of its Increments is in domain.ExecutionLost. Read it with the EXISTING batch ports u.IncrementsForRequirements (internal/application/ports.go:123) and u.ExecutionsForIncrements (:124), batched over exactly the ids on the page already read -- add NO port, edit NO store, and do not add a per-Requirement read loop. internal/reconciler/** is PROHIBITED: reconciler.recoverOne's actor is domain.NewActorID('reconciler'), a name the component makes up for itself, and internal/reconciler holds no application.Caller, so the Requirement transition cannot live there without giving it an identity it is not. Record, and do not assert, that an Execution in domain.ExecutionFailed rather than lost produces NO transition, and that docs/architecture/domain-model.md:275 says such a Requirement should become recovering, waiting or needs-input -- that is the recorded boundary, not a defect this task fixes.

A7. THE OBSERVATION MUST BE CARRIED, AND ITS ABSENCE MUST PRODUCE NOTHING. Every transition this pass issues records, on its own event, the observation that justified it: for waiting, the scheduler.Reason string and the decision's rank; for recovering, the Increment id and the Execution id that were lost; for completion, the candidate id and the bundle digest from the proof. Then, for EACH of the three, write a test that drives the pass with the justifying observation ABSENT and asserts ZERO transitions and the aggregate byte-identical by reflect.DeepEqual INCLUDING Version: capacity available and no contention for waiting; the Lease still active and the Execution still running for recovering; the promotion criteria unmet for completion. A pass that always advances is the defect these three tests exist to catch. Record no prompt, no provider output and no credential in any event or report field.

A8. STAGE D (the Increment creation path). For a Requirement whose domain status is domain.RequirementReady and whose scheduler.Decision has Assigned == true and which has no Increment in a non-terminal status, call the EXISTING Service.Plan and then the EXISTING Service.Prepare with the SAME scheduler context -- both already admit RoleScheduler (internal/application/service.go:888 and :1023), so no authority changes and internal/application/service.go stays unedited and PROHIBITED. Cap the number of Increments planned per pass at a named constant and report how many assignable Requirements were left unplanned. Assert: a Requirement the scheduler did NOT assign gets no Increment; a Requirement that already has a non-terminal Increment gets no second one; and with more assignable Requirements than the cap, exactly the cap is planned. Then assert the consequence that the DECLARATION-GAP ledger names: with the pass wired, a running control plane holds an Increment, and POST /v1/runner/claims:acquire for that Increment succeeds for an enrolled runner where before it could not.

A9. STAGE P (promotion), and the proof is obtained in exactly one way. Call release.Pipeline.Promote (internal/release/pipeline.go:38) and use the domain.StableReleaseProof it returns in GateResult.Proof. Do NOT call release.PromotionGate directly, do NOT call domain.CompletePromotionWithProof directly, do NOT store the proof, do NOT put it in a report field, do NOT log it and do NOT pass it across any package boundary other than into domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease. For each Requirement whose status is domain.RequirementActive and ALL of whose Increments are in domain.IncrementReleased, issue domain.RequirementEvaluate and then domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease with that proof IN THE SAME TRANSACTION, so a failure between them leaves the Requirement in neither evaluating nor completed. Assert the completed Requirement's StableSnapshot equals the promoted candidate's release id, version, bundle digest and evidence digest. internal/domain/**, internal/release/** and internal/reconciler/** are PROHIBITED; the shortest wrong answer -- exporting a proof constructor or making stableReleaseProofData settable -- requires opening a file this task may not touch.

A10. THE NEGATIVE THAT SEPARATES 'THE INCREMENT SUCCEEDED' FROM 'THE REQUIREMENT MAY COMPLETE'. In one table with two rows. ROW 1: drive a Requirement to active, plan an Increment, claim it, start and accept a SUCCEEDING Execution, carry the Increment to domain.IncrementReleased, and run the pass with a release candidate whose promotion criteria are UNMET -- a declared capability with no evidence, which internal/domain/release.go:98-102 refuses by name with ErrEvidenceIncomplete. Assert Pipeline.Promote errors, the report says refused with that reason, zero evaluations and zero completions were issued, and the Requirement is byte-identical by reflect.DeepEqual INCLUDING Version and INCLUDING StableSnapshot. ROW 2: promotion SUCCEEDS and returns a valid proof, but the Requirement's Increments are not all released -- assert no evaluate and no completion for that Requirement, while a SIBLING Requirement in the same pass whose Increments ARE all released does complete. Cite docs/architecture/domain-model.md:101 and docs/product/definition.md:130 in the test's own comment.

A11. THE SOURCE GUARD, AND ITS NON-VACUITY PROVEN BY EXECUTION. Add internal/application/completion_proof_guard_test.go, a go/ast scan modelled on the parse-and-scan structure of internal/scheduler/source_guard_test.go (parse with go/parser, FAIL OUTRIGHT on an empty file set so a broken glob cannot pass vacuously), walking every non-test .go file in the repository from the module root. Assert: the number of call sites of domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease is exactly ONE and it is in internal/application/loop.go; the number of call sites of release.Pipeline.Promote and of release.PromotionGate outside internal/release is exactly ONE and it is in internal/application/loop.go; and the number of files parsed is reported in the failure message so a shrunken scan is visible. THEN PROVE IT IS NOT VACUOUS, the way V2-087 did: delete the real call site, run the guard, record the RED verdict line and the exact failure message text, restore the call site, and record the GREEN verdict line, both with the argv. A guard never observed red is not evidence. Do NOT put these assertions in internal/application/source_guard_test.go or internal/application/requested_by_test.go -- both are PROHIBITED, and V2-086's single-producer scan in the latter must keep passing untouched, which you also re-run and record.

A12. THE BOUND, MEASURED, AND WHAT IT LEAVES UNEXAMINED. The pass makes a fixed set of bounded reads per invocation, none growing with the Requirement count: one u.RequirementsPage(ctx, req.Cursor, scheduler.MaxCandidates) -- keeping BOTH return values -- one u.RequirementRepositoryLinks batch over exactly those ids, one u.ActiveLeases(ctx, AllocationLeaseBound+1) which FAILS CLOSED above 100 with ErrAllocationLeaseBound (internal/application/allocation.go:88,93), one u.IncrementsForRequirements batch and one u.ExecutionsForIncrements batch over the same ids. BuildAllocationSnapshot fails closed above scheduler.MaxCandidates with ErrAllocationCandidateBound rather than truncating (allocation.go:455-458); preserve that -- do not catch it and continue. REQUIRED RECORD: the measured read and write counts of one pass, against quota.MutationUsage (Reads 32, Writes 16) and quota.ReadTransactionUsage (Reads 6001, Writes 1) and quota.DefaultBudget (Reads 25000, Writes 10000, Deletes 10000); an explicit statement of what one pass leaves unexamined, namely every Requirement after NextCursor; and how a later pass reaches it, namely the next tick carrying that cursor. REQUIRED TEST: seed more Requirements than one page, run two passes, and assert the second transitions a Requirement the first did not examine, and that MoreRequirementsExist is true on the first and correct on the second. Silent truncation that reads as 'covered everything' is the failure. internal/quota/** and internal/store/** are PROHIBITED: if a count does not fit, STOP and escalate; do not raise a budget and do not drop a read.

A13. THE OFFER READ AND ITS ROUTE. Measured: POST /v1/runner/claims:acquire requires a caller-supplied increment_id and expected_increment_version (internal/api/api.go:1079-1090, claimBody), the runner-role POST routes are exactly the four at internal/api/api.go:384-397, and there is NO runner-readable GET at all -- so a separate-process Runner cannot discover work by any means. Add Service.OfferedWork to internal/application/loop.go, gated runnerCaller(ctx) (internal/application/caller.go:110-118) so only a verified runner session may read it, derived from the SAME bounded page, returning at most a named cap of {requirement_id, increment_id, expected_increment_version} triples for Increments in domain.IncrementReady whose parent admits work. Add GET /v1/runner/work to internal/api/api.go using the file's existing routing idiom, gated to RoleRunner with 403 for an owner and 401 unauthenticated. Declare it in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml with an explicit response schema, additionalProperties false and explicit required lists. The response carries NO text, NO work packet, NO digest and NO field whose name contains password, credential, token, secret, raw_prompt or raw_provider_output; write no digest value anywhere in the contract. Do NOT edit contracts/release-contract/**, contracts/schemas/** or contracts/fixtures/**. Assert the route is not swallowed by any existing prefix branch, that a POST to it is not the route, and that an unauthenticated call is 401.

A14. THE RUNNER'S CONTROL-PLANE CLIENT, DETERMINISTIC AND STANDARD-LIBRARY ONLY. Add internal/runner/controlplane.go importing only the standard library (net/http, encoding/json, and what those need) plus internal/runner's own package types -- measured, internal/runner imports net/http in ZERO files today, so this introduces the dependency deliberately and it is intra-component: ci/components.json is NOT edited because the runner component's roots already contain both cmd/runner/** and internal/runner/**. The client takes an injected *http.Client and an injected clock, starts no goroutine and no timer, and exposes exactly four calls: read the offered work, acquire a claim, start an execution, report one heartbeat. The session token is read from a file the caller names, is sent only in the header the server reads, and appears in NO log line, NO error string and NO journal payload -- assert that by driving an error on every call and asserting the token substring is absent from every returned error and every written byte. Test it against a stub http.RoundTripper: do NOT use httptest.NewServer, which appears ZERO times in this repository and would introduce the goroutine determinism forbids. A non-2xx response is an error, never a retry loop; a malformed body is an error, never a zero value. Do NOT write a module-path string literal into any file -- concatenate a prefix with a suffix if you need one.

A15. THE REAL DRIVER, BOUNDED AND HONEST. Add internal/runner/loopdriver.go: for at most MaxDriverClaims offered Increments in one bounded pass, claim, create the real workspace through the existing runner.Workspace, append to the real fsync-backed runner.Journal, start the Execution, report one heartbeat, and STOP. It posts NO result: all three provider adapters return NoExec (internal/provider/adapters.go, re-measure) and no Provider CLI invocation is authorised for this task, so accepting a result would be accepting one it did not obtain. Assert by behaviour and by the new files' import allowlist that the driver never calls Provider.Run and never posts to /v1/executions/result. internal/runner/orchestrator.go and internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go are PROHIBITED: Orchestrator.RunFakeJourney stays byte-unchanged and test-only. RECORD the five measured differences from it: the real driver does not Capture (orchestrator.go:55 manufactures its own Requirement), does not fabricate a RoleRunner Caller (orchestrator.go:54 does, with no session verification), does not call Provider.Run (orchestrator.go:107 does), is bounded per pass, and shares no memory with the control plane. Confirm by measurement that RunFakeJourney still has exactly its pre-existing call sites and that internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go still passes unedited.

A16. cmd/runner STOPS BEING A STUB WITHOUT BREAKING WHAT IT ALREADY GUARANTEES. Keep `--version` printing exactly the version string on stdout before any other work, so `make smoke` is unaffected -- run `devbox run --pure -- make smoke` and record the verdict line, because a cmd/ binary changed. Keep the existing --fake mode and its refusal messages. Refuse, each with its own message and its own non-zero exit status and NONE of them containing the token: a relative or non-0700 data root, an absent or unreadable token file, a token file whose permissions are wider than 0600, an empty base URL, and a bound that is not positive. Add cmd/runner/main_test.go following the cmd/bootstrap/main_test.go idiom. A17. cmd/control-plane WIRING, INSIDE WHAT ALREADY EXISTS. Add the LoopPass call to the EXISTING InternalReconcile closure at cmd/control-plane/main.go:199-207, inside the EXISTING 5-second timeout at :200 and after the two existing ticks at :202 and :205, ordered so the lease-expiry pass has already produced the lost Executions stage R observes. The scheduler identity is already on the context (internal/api/api.go:114 and :119) -- do not construct one. Add the release-source wiring as a call to a new application-level constructor declared in internal/application/loop.go that takes a ROOT STRING, a repository and an environment class read from explicit environment variables and builds release.NewRouter and release.NewMemoryStore internally, then attaches the observer with Service.AttachReleaseObserver. cmd/control-plane must NOT import internal/release: measured, ci/components.json declares control-plane's dependencies as api, application, reconciler, runner and store-firestore, and adding release would be an edge that moves all 23 evidence keys. With the root UNCONFIGURED, assert that GET /v1/release/state still returns 503 with the same code through internal/api/api.go:900 and that the promotion stage reports skipped-not-configured -- an absent configuration is a skip, never a default root, for the reason internal/application/release_surface.go:17-23 already records.

A18. DETERMINISM IS ACCEPTANCE. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine and no randomness in any new or modified test. Every clock injected; the pass reads s.clock.Now() exactly once per invocation and passes that instant down. Every wait is a bounded deadline poll reusing an idiom already present in the file being edited -- in internal/api/live_local_test.go, the wait_for / wait_gone / wait_polls shape commit 56ee097 introduced on main after fixed-timeout waits in the lifecycle E2E had to be replaced for exactly this reason. A measured duration is logged as an observation and NEVER asserted as a threshold. Run every package with -race: `devbox run --pure -- go test -race -count=1 ./...`. If any new test needs to wait for the second process, wait on observable canonical state through a bounded poll, never on elapsed time.

A19. ADDITIVE, PROVEN BY MEASUREMENT. internal/domain, internal/release, internal/reconciler, internal/scheduler, internal/store, internal/quota, internal/provider, internal/web and internal/runner/orchestrator.go are byte-unchanged; ci/components.json and Makefile are unedited. Confirm each with `git diff --stat` scoped to the path and record the argv. No RequirementCommandKind, no RequirementStatus, no PermitKind, no port and no allowed() list is added or changed. No read-model change: confirm that nextAction (internal/application/readmodels.go:306-329) branches on completed and cancelled and on Execution and Increment status but never on waiting, recovering or evaluating, so a Requirement in any of the three continues to report exactly what it reports today -- record that as the reason readmodels.go is prohibited by design rather than by omission. Report before-and-after top-level test counts for every touched package and assert every pre-existing top-level test keeps its name and keeps passing. If the manifest check goes red, the design was DEPARTED FROM: stop and escalate rather than editing ci/** to make it green.

A20. THE EXECUTED PROOF AT preview-local, WITH TWO REAL PROCESSES. Extend TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive in internal/api/live_local_test.go -- which already starts the real cmd/control-plane binary in its own process group with runner.ProcessSupervisor (live_local_test.go:159) against the real Firestore emulator over real HTTP. Every wait is a bounded deadline poll on canonical state. Record: the environment class preview-local, the machine identifier, the emulator name and version, the go version resolved inside devbox run --pure, the devbox version, the worktree path, the branch, the base commit, and the two process identities. Run it and record the argv: `devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -race -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api`. devbox run --pure strips environment variables, so AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL must be passed with -e and never as a shell prefix. STATE PLAINLY in the record that the COMPLETION transition is NOT proven at this grade and why: the shipped configuration cannot assemble a fully-evidenced candidate and this task fabricates none.

A21. THE GRADE, AND THE SENTENCES THAT MAY NOT BE WRITTEN. State once, in every record: the reachability claims for waiting, for recovering, for Increment creation and for a separate-process Runner claiming and starting an Execution stop at environment class preview-local as release-contract.md:52 defines it -- the owner's own machine, the candidate version's Control Plane and Runner as real processes on localhost, a Firestore emulator as canonical store -- and the claim for the completion transition stops at COMPONENT (in-process) grade. release-contract.md:56 places the IAP authentication boundary, scale-to-zero, real Firestore permissions and contention, and the deploy path with D1, and v2-task-dag.md G3.3 says unit, fake, stub and contract evidence satisfies no real-environment condition at any grade. FORBIDDEN VERBATIM anywhere in the records, the commit messages or the report: 'observed on Cloud Run', 'Cloud Run revision', 'Cloud Logging', 'the deployed environment', 'production', 'a Stable promotion occurred', 'capability exercised', 'preview journey passed', and any capability id.
